result.title: LoRA Superposition across Pretrained Models
result.summary: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is usually tied to the pretrained backbone on which it is learned. We ask whether LoRAs trained independently for the same task on different pretrained backbones can be summed and applied unchanged to all contributing backbones. We call this construction LoRA superposition. Across seven ViT-B/16 CLIP backbones and eight image-classification tasks, the exact sum improves all 56 backbone-task pairs and achieves a mean accuracy gain of 30.21 percentage points over the unadapted backbone. The exact sum achieves a mean accuracy only 0.28 percentage points below that of individually trained solo LoRAs. In contrast, a leave-one-model-out (LOMO) sum produces a mean gain of only 0.06 percentage points over the unadapted backbones. Backbone-specific solo LoRAs are nearly orthogonal in parameter space, while pairwise cross-backbone responses are strongly concentrated on the diagonal. These results support a component-wise non-interference hypothesis, under which the frozen backbone acts as an implicit selector of its own component without explicit routing or cross-model alignment.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「LoRA superposition」，考察在不同预训练主干上为同一任务独立训练的 LoRA 能否直接相加并原样适用于所有贡献主干；在 7 个 ViT-B/16 CLIP 主干与 8 个图像分类任务上，精确求和几乎追平单独训练的 LoRA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「参数近正交、组件互不干扰、冻结主干充当隐式选择器」的加法组合思路，或可为 LVR 中多能力或多 latent 假设模块的免路由组合与贡献分配提供核查线索，但迁移性需较多验证。
